What is Atom SDK

One sentence explanation

ATOM SDK is a client library that lets you control ATOM software from code - create and edit visual processing graphs, or use ready-made graphs as execution engines.

what problem does it solve

The ATOM software exposes a large number of interfaces through the HTTP service for managing and executing vision processing processes. There are several pain points in directly calling these interfaces for development:

  • HTTP The request format is complex and needs to be written by hand every time JSON Construction and response parsing

  • Diagram editing needs to carry timestamp to prevent concurrency conflicts, and manual management is prone to errors.

  • The input frame at runtime has a special binary protocol, which makes manual packaging cumbersome and has a high probability of error.

  • File parameters require special multipart upload logic

SDK encapsulates these details, allowing you to focus on business logic.

The core package of SDK

  • Automatic Timestamp management: Each time the diagram is opened or modified, the server returns a new timestamp, and subsequent editing operations must carry it to avoid being rejected. SDK is automatically cached and carried after each successful response. In most cases, manual processing is not required. For details, see What is Timestamp.

  • Binary protocol processing: RuntimeService.run_graph Normal mode needs to package multi-frame images + point clouds in a specific format. SDK provides RuntimeFrame for automatic completion; passive binocular passive_bino mode needs to send complete EPICRAW3, SDK provides RuntimePassiveBinoFrame and corresponding factory methods, see Runtime input frames (RuntimeFrame / RuntimePassiveBinoFrame) for details.

  • File upload: When setting node parameters, if the parameter value is a local file (model file, configuration file, etc.), SDK will automatically upload it in the multipart format, without the need to manually read the file or construct a request.

  • Mixed response decoding: Some interfaces (such as reading port data) return JSON + binary mixed response, SDK automatically decodes and merges binary attachments into the result dictionary.

what it is not

  • Not a front end for Atom: SDK does not provide UI, only provides API calling capabilities

  • Not a graph design tool: The visual design of graphs needs to be completed on the Atom front-end

  • Not a stand-alone service: SDK must be used with running ATOM software

Typical usage scenarios

  • Automated graph editing: Batch update model files to different graph nodes - use SDK to write scripts to automatically open graphs, find nodes, upload files, and run verification.

  • External system integration: Send image/point cloud data to Atom for processing and get back the results. Use RuntimeFrame for ordinary images + point clouds, EPICRAW3 for passive binocular images; use RuntimeService to load pre-designed images, and call run_graph to execute and read the results every time data comes.

  • Automated testing: Use SDK to create a standard test chart, set parameters, run, and verify whether the output meets expectations.
